claims.text: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy has inherently high lattice distortion.
FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy exhibits sluggish diffusion.
High lattice distortion and sluggish diffusion accelerate formation and reconstitution of a protective oxide layer in the HEA.
The protective oxide layer is dense and nanocrystalline.
The protective oxide layer is predominantly composed of Al2O3 and Cr2O3.
The HEA oxide layer rapidly reforms after mechanical disruption.
Rapid oxide reformation minimizes direct exposure of the underlying metal during wear.
Minimizing direct metal exposure reduces synergistic damage from mechanical abrasion and localized corrosion.
A conventional stainless-steel baseline has a thinner, less robust oxide film than the FeCoNiCrAl HEA.
Under moderate-load tribocorrosion conditions, the HEA will have a lower wear rate than the stainless-steel baseline.
Under moderate-load tribocorrosion conditions, the HEA will have a lower corrosion current density than the stainless-steel baseline.
In situ measurements will show continuous and rapid oxide-layer reformation in the HEA.
Under the same conditions, the stainless-steel baseline will exhibit progressive degradation of its oxide film.
The proposed protective mechanism should operate under moderate mechanical stresses at 25–50°C in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
The protective effect may fail when mechanical disruption outpaces oxide-layer regeneration, such as under extreme load or high temperature.
